title: Find a Pair With Target Sum in a Sorted Array
statement: Given a sorted integer array nums and an integer target, return true if there exists a pair whose sum equals target.
mnemonic: Too small -> left++, too large -> right--
think: What is the task asking? Determine whether any pair adds up to target.
What is the key operation? Use sorted order to move inward intelligently.
What wording signals stand out? Sorted array, pair, target sum.
What is the brute force idea? Check every pair with nested loops.
What is the better/optimal idea? Start at both ends and adjust based on the current sum.
What are the edge cases? No valid pair, duplicate values, negative numbers.
What is the complexity? O(n) time and O(1) space.
How would I explain it in an interview? I use the sorted property: if the sum is too small, move left; if too large, move right.
interview: I would use two pointers because the array is sorted. That lets me move inward based on whether the current sum is too small or too large.
ru: Отсортированность даёт главное преимущество: если сумма мала, двигаем левый указатель; если велика — правый.
visualExplanation:
nums = [1,2,4,6,10], target = 8
1+10=11 too big -> right--
1+6=7 too small -> left++
2+6=8 -> true

critical: Miss that array is sorted and use O(n^2)
important: Move wrong pointer after comparing sum

gaps: Important: recognize sorted pair => two pointers
Nice to have: explain pointer decision logic fluently
constraints: Assume nums is sorted in ascending order.
whyThisPattern: This is a Two Pointers problem because sorted order lets us make directional decisions from both ends.
whyNotOtherPatterns: Not Dictionary, because sorted order gives a simpler O(1)-space solution.
Not Sliding Window, because we are not working with a contiguous segment sum.
